title: session-meld: keepalive token-lease and pullstream interface harmonization across Python/TS/Go
author: Riley Chen
release_notes: Polish: unify token-lease keepalive and pullstream async iterator surface across SDKs; bump Python/TS/Go SDK packages. Backwards-compatible shim included for older consumers.
description: Context: Several customers and internal e2e tests surfaced subtle races between token refresh timing and long-lived streaming consumers (pull/push streams). This PR harmonizes the ergonomic surface for a token lease / keepalive abstraction and updates the pullstream async-iterator shape consistently across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: reduce surprising reconnects, simplify application-level token lifecycle, and make cross-language examples portable. Changes: 1) Introduce a minimal TokenLease interface with keepalive() and expire_at() helpers and a light-weight TokenProxy shim for older credential providers. 2) Add a PullStreamAdapter/AsyncPullIterator facade in each SDK that exposes a consistent next_chunk()/close() pattern and emits explicit "lease_refreshed" events for observability. 3) Centralize retry/backoff integration so stream consumer retries defer to configured retry profiles (short-circuit for idempotent snapshots). 4) Slight API surface bumps (minor semver) and packaging/version updates: python->1.14.0, typescript->1.9.2, go->v0.8.5. Compatibility: a backwards-compatible TokenProxy shim is provided so existing credential providers continue to work; docs and migration notes included. Checklist: - [x] design doc and cross-SDK API sketches (linked in PR) - [x] Python implementation and unit/integration tests - [x] TypeScript implementation and browser/node tests - [x] Go implementation and concurrent stream smoke tests - [x] end-to-end test against hosted staging with long-lived stream scenarios - [x] docs + changelogs updated - [x] version bumps and CI green Related: ENG-4021 (stream-resilience), ENG-3908 (cred-session-leases).

review_comments: Aisha: Can we avoid a second goroutine in Go by using a context-aware ticker? The current implementation spawns a refresher goroutine per stream which might be heavy under extreme fanout. -- Riley: I've changed the goroutine to use a shared lease manager for sessions with >1 active streams; see packages/sdk-go/stream/lease_manager.go (added) in the follow-up commit.

Miguel: In TS, how does next_chunk() differ from the existing iterator.next() semantics? Will it break for existing for-await-of usage? -- Riley: next_chunk() preserves async iterator semantics; a for-await-of wrapper is provided. Migration section in docs shows both patterns.

Lena: race on close() observed in go unit test when token expires during send; request that we add an explicit close handshake. -- Riley: Added an edge-case test and a close handshake (pullstream_adapter.go) that drains the send path before canceling the lease refresher.

Aisha: please add a telemetry dimension for 'lease_refresh_outcome' (success/failure/latency bucket). -- Riley: telemetry metric added to python/ts/go adapters and wired to console tracing; see observability note in docs.
